$comment: Per-package `-race` wall-clock budgets, enforced by scripts/check-race-budget.mjs on the release tier only (.github/workflows/bazel-linux-smoke.yml) and runnable locally via `make check-race-budget`. Every figure below names the harness that produced it: a second measured one way is not a second measured another, and re-deriving a budget from the wrong regime silently defeats the ratchet. See docs/plans/BOS-1022-bossd-race-test-tax.md.
budgetRegime: bazel test --config=race --nocache_test_results; each target's per-shard wall clock (Build Event Protocol testAttemptDurationMillis) summed across its shards
$regimeNote: budgetSeconds is compared ONLY against bazelSummedPostFixSeconds-style figures. The native `go test -race -count=1` figures are recorded because they are what BOS-1022 set out to reduce and what the plan's before/after table quotes, but they are NOT the enforced regime: summing per-shard wall clock adds each shard's own process startup and schema build to the same total work, so a Bazel-summed figure is systematically larger than its native counterpart. Requiring budgetSeconds < nativePreFixSeconds is therefore a deliberately conservative cross-regime bound — it also holds against the (larger, unmeasured) Bazel-summed pre-fix figure, so a budget that passes validation could not have passed before the fix.
$calibration: bazelSummedPostFixSeconds was measured on an Apple M-series laptop, the only race-capable host this branch could run, with `make check-race-budget`. bazelSummedPostFixSecondsSecondRun is an independent run of the same command on the same host: the two differ by up to 16%, which is the run-to-run noise floor for a sharded race suite competing for cores, and is why a budget near the measured figure would flake. The CI runner (ubicloud-standard-8) is slower again, so budgets carry roughly 2.5x headroom over the local figure rather than the ~1.2x a same-host, low-noise calibration would justify. That makes this a coarse ratchet: it catches a return to per-test migration replay (a 3-4x regression), not a 20% drift. Tighten it once the release tier has published a real CI figure — see the BOS-1022 plan follow-ups.
$unshardedNote: bazelUnshardedSeconds is one `bazel test --config=race --nocache_test_results --test_sharding_strategy=disabled --local_test_jobs=1` run on the same kind of laptop (2026-10-19), taken when shard_count was removed from these targets. With one shard the summed figure is the whole run, so it compares to budgetSeconds directly; the sharded sums above it were larger because each shard paid its own startup.

targets.label: //services/bossd/internal/db:db_test
targets.note: The package BOS-1022 was filed against. Pre-fix cost was goose replaying every migration per test under -race checkptr; dbtest.Schema now builds the schema once per test binary.

targets.label: //services/bossd/internal/server:server_test
targets.note: Same migration tax, reached through the server package's own DB fixtures; now routed through dbtest.

targets.label: //services/bossd/internal/session:session_test
targets.note: Sleep-bound rather than migration-bound: the fix replaced fixed sleeps with waits on the outcome. Budgeted so a reintroduced sleep shows up.

targets.label: //services/boss/internal/views:views_test
targets.note: Seeded property sweeps, not migrations. Four of them were 105.9s of the 143.2s native race run; the per-PR suite now runs a prefix of each and the nightly native job the whole sequence (BOSS_VIEWS_SWEEPS). Sharded 4 ways before, the shards summed to 166.3s under --config=race. Budgeted at 2.5x so the full sweeps creeping back into the per-PR suite fail here.
